propositions: A class with an unreachable primary model (downed local endpoint, throttled provider) fails the gate entirely because there is no fallback mechanism; the system should permit inline fallback model configs to be tried sequentially

pydantic-ai's FallbackModel wrapper must be constructed with a narrowed fallback_on predicate that fires only on errors where switching providers helps (availability/rate-limit classes), not on auth or input-size errors, because provider SDK retry logic can delay failover by ~60s

FallbackModel submodels must be entered/exited as an async context manager sharing a single ProviderSession so all clients (pydantic-ai-created and rebar-created transports) are managed in one lifecycle without double-close or leaks

A fallback entry carrying a custom endpoint must produce a model object built against that endpoint, not one silently built against the provider default, to enable the main use case of a local OpenAI-compatible proxy as a fallback

Capabilities, cache settings, and tool guards must be computed from the resolved candidate list (primary plus all fallbacks) as the conservative intersection before the FallbackModel wrapper exists, because FallbackModel.provider returns None and calling capabilities_for on it would silently yield incorrect values

provider_provenance must record the ordered candidates and the ran_model read from ModelResponse (not FallbackModel.model_name), so a verdict produced by a fallback correctly attests which model actually answered rather than misattributing to the primary
